passage:
In their Copenhagen flat, Anders, two, was stacking wooden blocks into a wobbly tower, tongue between his teeth. "Anders! Bath time!" his father, Emil, called from the hallway. Nothing. "Anders!" Louder. The tower grew one block taller.
Emil felt a flash of irritation, then came and knelt beside him and touched his shoulder. Anders looked up, surprised, as if he had only now noticed his papa. "Tower!" he said proudly.
"Big tower," Emil agreed. "One more block, then bath."

qa.q: What was Anders building?
qa.a: Anders was stacking wooden blocks into a wobbly tower.

qa.q: Why didn't Anders answer when Emil called?
qa.a: He was so absorbed in the tower that the call didn't reach him; his surprised look shows he truly hadn't noticed, not that he was ignoring his papa.

qa.q: What worked for Emil?
qa.a: Going close, touching Anders gently, sharing interest in the tower, and giving one small step before bath.

qa.q: How might the evening go if Emil kept calling from the hallway?
qa.a: Emil would likely get more irritated, and Anders might be startled or upset when finally pulled away, turning bath time into a fight.

grounding: It shows a toddler so absorbed in his blocks that he does not hear his name, a normal attention limit rather than defiance.

passage: I'm Himani, Pallavi's neighbour. Yesterday on the building lawn, her son Neel, who is two, was pouring sand from one cup into another, again and again. Pallavi called, "Neel, come, let's go home," three times. He didn't even turn his head. I thought he was being stubborn. Then she walked over and tapped him, and he jumped a little and smiled at her as if she had just appeared. I don't think he had heard her at all.

qa.q: What was Neel doing on the building lawn?
qa.a: Neel was pouring sand from one cup into another, again and again.

qa.q: What does Neel's little jump and smile when tapped suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: Neel was startled and then happy to see Pallavi, which suggests he was so absorbed in the sand that he hadn't heard her at all; he wasn't being stubborn.

qa.q: What could Pallavi do first the next time she needs Neel's attention?
qa.a: Walk over, get down to his level and touch him gently before speaking, since calling from far away may not reach him.

qa.q: How did Himani's view of Neel change?
qa.a: Himani first thought he was being stubborn, then saw his surprised smile and realised he hadn't heard at all.

grounding: It shows a toddler so absorbed in pouring sand that he does not hear his name, which a neighbour first mistakes for stubbornness.

passage:
Monday: Gautam, two, sat stirring a toy pot. Nikita called him for lunch twice, then snapped, "Why don't you listen?" He burst into tears.
Wednesday: Nikita watched him lining up cars and remembered how deep he goes. She sat beside him first and waited.
Friday: She touched his back, waited for his eyes, then said, "Lunch, Gautam." He looked up and came, still holding a car.

qa.q: What was Gautam doing on Monday when Nikita called him?
qa.a: Gautam sat stirring a toy pot.

qa.q: Why did Gautam burst into tears on Monday?
qa.a: He probably hadn't heard the calls at all, so the sudden snap felt frightening and confusing to him.

qa.q: What changed in Nikita's approach by Friday?
qa.a: She touched his back and waited for his eyes before speaking, getting his attention first instead of calling across the room.

qa.q: What would change if Nikita still believed Gautam was ignoring her?
qa.a: She would keep snapping, Gautam would keep crying, and mealtimes would turn into fights over something that isn't defiance.

grounding: It shows a toddler absorbed in play who does not hear his name, and a mother learning it is a normal limit rather than defiance.

passage: In their Bhopal flat, two-year-old Rayyan sat on the rug, pushing a yellow truck under the sofa and pulling it out again. "Rayyan! Lunch!" Zeenat called from the kitchen. He didn't look up. Dilnaz, his big sister, rolled her eyes. "He's ignoring you, Ammi." Zeenat came over, knelt beside him and touched his shoulder. Rayyan looked up, blinked, and smiled as if seeing her for the first time. "Truck," he said, holding it out.

qa.q: What was Rayyan doing with the yellow truck?
qa.a: Pushing it under the sofa and pulling it out again.

qa.q: How did Rayyan seem to feel while playing with the truck, and what shows it?
qa.a: Rayyan seemed happy and completely absorbed in the truck, so he didn't hear the call, and he smiled and held the truck out when Zeenat touched his shoulder.

qa.q: What did Zeenat do that worked better than calling louder?
qa.a: She came over, knelt beside him and touched his shoulder, which gently brought his attention from the truck to her.

qa.q: Why might Dilnaz think Rayyan was ignoring Ammi?
qa.a: From an older child's view, not answering looks like choosing not to listen, so Dilnaz reads it as defiance rather than a toddler's absorbed attention.

grounding: A toddler boy absorbed in his truck does not hear his mother call, a normal limit of attention that his sister mistakes for defiance.

passage:
"Advait! Shoes on, we're going to the park!"
Advait, two, didn't move. He was dropping pebbles into a steel glass, one by one.
"See, Trisha?" said Deepika, his Masi. "He's being stubborn."
"I don't think so, Didi. Watch." Trisha, his mother, crouched until her face was near the glass. "Clink," she said softly.
Advait looked up. "Clink!"
"One more clink, then shoes?"
He dropped a pebble, grinned, and held out his foot.
"So he just didn't hear?" said Deepika.
"His whole head was in that glass."

qa.q: What was Advait dropping into the steel glass?
qa.a: Pebbles, one by one.

qa.q: How did Advait seem to feel while dropping pebbles, and what shows it?
qa.a: Advait seemed content and absorbed in the pebbles and the glass, not stubborn; when Trisha said "Clink" he joined in, grinned and held out his foot.

qa.q: What did Trisha do that got Advait's attention, and why did it work?
qa.a: She crouched near the glass and joined his game with a soft "clink", meeting his focus first and then gently turning it to shoes.

qa.q: How does Deepika's view of Advait change during the scene?
qa.a: She starts out thinking he is being stubborn, then sees he simply didn't hear because he was absorbed.

grounding: A toddler boy absorbed in dropping pebbles does not hear his name, and his mother shows it is a limit of attention, not defiance.
